question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Estado da India — Headquarters / Centre of Power]
options: Estado da India — Goa was its capital from 1510
Estado da India — Governed by a Viceroy or Governor appointed by the Portuguese Crown
Estado da India — Calicut (Kozhikode) served as the administrative capital of the Estado
Estado da India — Encompassed Portuguese possessions in Asia and East Africa
wrong_fact: Calicut was never the capital. Goa, captured in 1510, became the capital and remained the seat of the Estado da India.
explanation: The Estado da India was the collective name for Portuguese possessions in Asia and East Africa, administered from Goa (from 1510 onwards). A Viceroy or Governor-General appointed by Lisbon headed the administration. Calicut (Kozhikode) was an important trading city but was the seat of the Zamorin — not a Portuguese administrative capital.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Estado da India — Geographic Extent and Key Possessions]
options: Diu — Portuguese possession on the Gujarat coast, key to controlling northern Arabian Sea trade
Hormuz — Portuguese-controlled strait linking the Persian Gulf to the Arabian Sea
Malacca — Portuguese conquest (1511) gave control over the Straits of Malacca
Aden — Portuguese successfully captured Aden in 1513, securing the Red Sea entrance
wrong_fact: Aden was never captured by the Portuguese. Afonso de Albuquerque attempted to take Aden in 1513 but failed, allowing the Ottomans and Egyptians to retain influence over Red Sea trade.
explanation: The Estado da India's strategic pillars were Goa (capital), Hormuz (Persian Gulf), Malacca (Southeast Asia), and Diu (Gujarat coast). Aden was a critical Red Sea port that Albuquerque tried but failed to capture in 1513; this failure meant the Portuguese could never fully strangle the spice route through the Red Sea and Egypt.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Estado da India — Viceroys/Governors and their Territories]
options: Francisco de Almeida — First Governor of Portuguese India, focused on Blue Water Policy (Cartaz system at sea)
Afonso de Albuquerque — Second Governor, captured Goa (1510), Malacca (1511), and Hormuz (1515)
Nuno da Cunha — Governor who captured Diu through the Battle of Diu (1538) against the Ottoman-Gujarat alliance
Lopo Soares de Albergaria — Governor who ordered destruction of Hindu temples in Goa and began systematic religious persecution
wrong_fact: Nuno da Cunha was the Governor during the first Battle of Diu (1538), but Portugal did not 'capture' Diu in 1538 — they defeated the Ottoman-Gujarat fleet but Diu was formally ceded to Portugal only in 1535 under an earlier treaty. The 1538 battle was a defence against reconquest, not a fresh capture.
explanation: The Battle of Diu in 1538 was fought to defend Portuguese positions against an Ottoman-Egyptian-Gujarat confederacy fleet. Diu had been leased to Portugal by the Gujarat Sultanate in 1535 via a treaty with Bahadur Shah. Nuno da Cunha was the governor who negotiated this treaty. The 1538 battle (naval) decisively confirmed Portuguese naval supremacy. The option is misleading by saying he 'captured' Diu through that battle.
